title: Uniqueness of linear threshold functions
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued. Suppose $f$ is a polynomial threshold function of degree at most one. If their Fourier–Walsh coefficients agree at every subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|S|\le1$, then $g=f$.
hypotheses_covered: dimension n is a natural number
f is a polynomial threshold function of degree at most one
Fourier–Walsh coefficients of f and g agree for every subset of size at most one
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E_x[h(x)\chi_S(x)]$ for uniform $x$, subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$.
Suppose $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(a_\varnothing+\sum_{i=1}^na_i(-1)^{x_i})$ for real coefficients, where $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
If $\widehat g(S)=\widehat f(S)$ whenever $|S|\le1$, then $g=f$.
